posts.text: What are you exploring with Claude this weekend?
A pop-up city where each building is a paper fold drawn on a flat canvas, Sonnet 5.5.
A jet engine in interactive 3D you can cut away and pull apart, made with Opus 5.5.
A pixel walk through Seattle that follows the real weather and time of day.
Claude Code and a camera, left running overnight on Old Street.
Poems, illustrated in Claude Code.
Water, simulated in the browser.
A 3D site that flies you from outside the Milky Way down to Jupiter’s moons, Opus 5.5.
Embossed cards, made with Opus 5.5.
Lots of inventive things made with Claude these past few weeks. A few of our favorites: A working watermill, built with Opus 5.5.

We're adding a new plugin to Claude Code: You should Know. It scans Claude's output for important information you might miss to help keep you in the loop. Enable it with: /plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin

"You should know" is a mod that works by spinning off a sideagent to observe Claude's output. Read more about mods in our newest blog post: https://claude.dev/blog/getting-started-with-claude-code-mods/

Applies automatically each time you create a design, deck, or doc, and runs through October 15 on Pro, Max, and Team plans. How it works and full terms: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17274727

For two weeks, start a design, deck, or doc in the Claude app, and the work that follows in that conversation uses 50% less of your usage limits. Give it a try with Claude Sonnet 5.5. It has a strong eye for design and builds slides that need minimal editing.
We’ve used mods to build features like /diff and AGENTS.md support. We hope you find them as useful (and fun) as we do, and can't wait to see what you build! https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-mods

We're adding pre-built sample mods to the Claude Code Playground repo you can riff off of, if you need some inspiration. Learn more in our getting started guide: https://claude.dev/blog/getting-started-with-claude-code-mods/

You can now mod Claude Code: - Change how it behaves - Customize the UI - Swap in your own features Write one with a few lines of TypeScript, or have Claude build it for you. Mods ship inside plugins, so you install them with /plugin in the CLI or desktop app. A few examples:
https://Claude.dev is our new home for developers building with Claude. You'll find engineering deep dives, Claude Code and API guides, tips from the teams building Claude, and some fun easter eggs.
Register for San Francisco: https://www.anthropic.com/events/claude-founder-house-san-francisco Register for Stockholm: https://www.anthropic.com/events/claude-founder-house-stockholm

Claude Founder House is coming to SF Tech Week (Oct 6–8) and Stockholm (Oct 14). Come for talks, workshops, and office hours with our team, plus time to meet others building with Claude. Whether you're a founder, a CEO, or a builder, there's a session for you.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 is out! We wrote a guide for building with it: • choosing between Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 • migrating from Sonnet 5 and tuning effort • using it in Claude Code https://claude.dev/blog/building-with-claude-sonnet-5-5/

Claude can now help you build evaluations and hillclimb on them. In this article, we share guidance on eval design & skills that Claude Code can use to improve your applications. https://claude.dev/blog/automating-eval-design-and-hillclimbing/
Bouncing-ball physics tests by @forwardeditor from the same prompt, Sonnet 5 vs Sonnet 5.5.
What are you exploring with Sonnet 5.5?
@LEJ_limited gave Sonnet 5.5 a 60×46 pixel emoji and asked for a 3D model he could print. A few hours later, it was on his desk.
A thread of early experiments with Claude Sonnet 5.5. A fall foliage simulator by @_re_pete, made with Sonnet 5 vs Sonnet 5.5.

We’re extending preserved thinking with Sonnet 5.5 to curb distillation attacks via account-switching. Thinking stays in the original org that generated it, so if you switch accounts mid-session, Claude will reread the session and generate new thinking. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking

Sonnet 5.5 is available now in the Claude Platform and Claude Code. We granted all Pro, Max, and Team users a reset last Tuesday. If you haven’t used it yet, you can still apply it whenever you want, before Oct 22. https://clau.de/reset

Sonnet 5.5 is smarter, more efficient, and 30% faster than Sonnet 5. It costs up to 30% less for most work, so your Claude Code usage goes further too. Use it for well-scoped everyday tasks like fixing bugs and quickly iterating on features.

On our automated behavioral audit, Sonnet 5.5 improves on or matches Sonnet 5 on most measures of alignment and honesty. It’s also the first Sonnet model with cyber safeguards and fallbacks like those on our most capable models. Routine software development is unaffected.

Pitch rate of ~12°/s to hit 35° in 3 s at cruise speed demands ~5 g centripetal accel, so n ≈ −4 g. That exceeds the 737’s −1 g structural limit and available elevator authority. Realistic rates of a few deg/s still need sustained low/near-zero lift for many seconds to curve the path from level. The 0.5 a t² term is simply the integrated vertical displacement from initial vy≈0 under that acceleration; it is not “added on top.” Once steep, +0.8 G is possible, but the bulk of the 14 kft loss occurs while the trajectory is still steepening.

No. Male lions are physically stronger and larger (typically 150-250 kg vs. females 120-180 kg), with more muscle mass and a protective mane for fights. Lionesses often appear dominant because prides are built around related females who handle most hunting, cub-rearing, and daily decisions. Groups of them confront males (especially to protect cubs from new rivals), and females can get assertive during mating. Males focus on territorial defense.
